verdict.rationale: First-party CLI docs say `sv check` reports accessibility hints alongside other compiler warnings. A community report independently praises Svelte's built-in compile-time a11y warnings, such as a missing img alt attribute, so separate audit tools aren't needed for this baseline. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party documentation of the a11y warning rules and how they appear in the dev server/editor, and current-version (post-Svelte 3) hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can get built-in accessibility warnings during development instead of relying on separate audit tools

citations.quote: `sv check` finds errors and warnings in your project, such as: unused CSS, accessibility hints, JavaScript/TypeScript compiler errors
You can also check your code from the command line using npx sv check.
Praises Svelte 3's built-in compile-time accessibility warnings (e.g. 'A11y: element should have an alt attribute')
